nodes.description: Upper lip fusion needs more cadherin adhesion than neighbouring tissue does, so a general reduction in surface cadherin crosses that tissue's threshold while leaving others above theirs. This is the node that explains the syndrome's selectivity: a gene expressed throughout the embryonic epithelium produces a malformation concentrated in the lip, palate, eyelid margins and tooth-forming epithelium. Fusion itself is driven by actomyosin contractility along multicellular F-actin cables anchored at the fusion site, and attenuating that contractility pharmacologically or genetically also produces cleft lip.

nodes.description: Tooth development fails in the dental lamina, giving severe agenesis and abnormal crown form. This is deliberately not filed as a fusion failure: the lip, palate and eyelid phenotypes are failures of two epithelial sheets meeting, where tooth agenesis is a failure of the dental lamina to initiate and shape a tooth germ. What the two have in common is the reduced cadherin adhesion upstream, not the morphogenetic event.

nodes.description: About half the normal amount of p120-catenin. The protein's relevant job is to bind the cadherin cytoplasmic juxtamembrane domain and so prevent cadherin endocytosis. Mouse genetics has since narrowed which of p120-catenin's several functions matters here: binding to RhoA and to Kaiso is dispensable during mammalian development, while stabilisation of cadherins is crucial. That result is why this entry does not model the Wnt and Kaiso transcriptional branch as a parallel disease mechanism.

nodes.description: A frameshift deletion segregating through three generations of a Chinese pedigree, carried by the grandfather, the father and two offspring, so it is one of the transmitted rather than de novo CTNND1 alleles. The pedigree carries two further findings that are not part of this disease and should not be read as part of it: the elder brother's hearing loss is attributed to double heterozygous GJB2 and GJB3 variants, and a de novo 1.46 Mb 17q12 microdeletion in the mother is attributed to her bilateral renal cysts.
